texts: An anterior infarction, the arrow in the front of the stag's chest, lowers the ejection fraction far more than an inferior one, the arrow from underneath: C.
The LAD feeds a large part of the left ventricle, its front wall, apex and septum, so losing it cripples the pump, the bouncer who now ejects only a trickle.
An inferior infarct damages less muscle, yet even a small posterolateral infarct can distort the subvalvular apparatus and cause ischaemic mitral regurgitation.
Ischaemic regurgitation does not depend on global dilatation alone, and a ventricle larger than about 65 mm makes reverse remodelling less likely, not more.
Memory hook: the arrow in the front empties the bouncer's counter; the arrow from below barely moves it.
